guide.title: Guide
guide.basics:
GOAL: make your opponent fall — drive their BALANCE to 0. There is no HP.

YOUR TURN: you get {energy} energy and draw {hand} cards. The yellow circle on a card is its energy cost. Tap a card to play it (on a phone: the first tap enlarges it, the second plays it). Unplayed cards are discarded at the end of the turn; when the draw pile is empty, the discard pile is shuffled back in. A greyed-out card can't be played right now — its red label says why.

PALM SAVE ✋: in bökh your palms may touch the ground, but not your knee, elbow or back. Once per match, a hit that would make you fall leaves you at {palm} balance instead.

FATIGUE: bökh has no time limit, so from turn {fatigue} both wrestlers lose balance at the start of every turn — 1 at first, +1 more every {every} turns.

THE RUN: beat {rounds} opponents in a row. After each win you pick a new move for your deck and recover {heal} balance. Your balance carries over between matches. One loss ends the run.
guide.grip:
GRIP is shared by both wrestlers. It rises step by step: 0 Distance → 1 One-hand → 2 Two-hand → 3 Clinch. The wrestlers step closer as it rises.

Your throws need grip — the higher the grip, the stronger the throw. But the opponent's attacks need grip too! If their attack needs more grip than there is, they can only grab (grip +{fallback}) instead.

So raising grip opens your throws — and theirs. Lowering grip (Step Back) can cancel their throw.
guide.opponents:
The opponent's NEXT MOVE is always shown at the top: ⚔ attack, 🛡 brace (gains guard), ✊ grab (grip up). If their attack lacks grip, the panel says so and they will only grab.

Each opponent repeats a fixed pattern — learn it and prepare. Opponents are heavier than you (more balance), but they have no palm save, they never adapt, and you always see what's coming.
guide.defense:
GUARD 🛡 absorbs damage from attacks. It resets at the start of your next turn, so play it on the turn the attack is coming. The opponent's Brace works the same way and lasts through your turn — your throws hit their guard first.

REVERSAL ↺: if the opponent attacks this turn, the attack is cancelled and its full damage hits them instead. Wasted if they don't attack.

Self-damage (Sacrifice Throw) and fatigue ignore guard.

If both wrestlers fall at the same moment, the one with lower balance loses. On a tie, you lose.
guide.combosIntro: There is no special combo rule — combos come from playing the right cards together:
combo.legHook: {legGrab} → {hook}: from Distance, reach Two-hand grip and throw in the same turn ({cost} energy, {dmg} damage).
combo.slap: {slap} first: it's free and gives +{n} energy next turn — enough for a grip card and {hook} together.
combo.lift: {legGrab} + {sleeveGrip} → {lift}: build to Clinch, then land the biggest throw in the game ({dmg} damage).
combo.hip: {hipThrow}: {dmg} damage, then grip drops to One-hand — so a Two-hand attack coming next turn fails.
combo.knee: {kneeSweep} + {lowerStance}: shrink the coming attack by {w} and block {g} more.
combo.stepReversal: {stepBack} or {reversal} against a big throw: Step Back drops grip so the throw fails; Reversal throws its whole damage back at them.
tipguide.1: Look at the opponent's next move BEFORE playing cards. Attack coming? Guard, step back or reverse. Brace or grab coming? Spend the turn throwing.
tipguide.2: Don't throw into a big guard — the guard absorbs your damage first. Build grip or guard on those turns instead.
tipguide.3: The opponent grabs too. If they are about to grab, you may need one grip card less next turn.
tipguide.4: Save the palm save. Taking a hit to 1 balance early leaves you nothing for later.
tipguide.5: Fatigue hurts both wrestlers. If you are ahead on balance, a long fight favours you; if behind, push hard before turn {fatigue}.
tipguide.6: Balance carries over between matches, and a win only restores {heal}. Winning cleanly matters for the next fight.
